page: Microsoft Azure D8pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution across 8 vCPUs. It features 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration with AES support. The instance includes no bundled local storage and contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations show steady throughput across general compute tasks, highlighted by single-threaded gzip compression achieving 33.13 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile. General computing tests, such as Geekbench multi-core at 9492.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 16568.19, exhibit consistent mid-tier capability. Passmark CPU encryption scored 1511.24 in the lower quartile, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing using a 7B model registered in the bottom decile at 12.34 tokens per second. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth measures 167.61 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 72.69 GB/sec.

With its dedicated ARM cores and reduced memory allocation per vCPU, the instance offers resource density for compute-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools or heavy local scratch disks. It provides consistent throughput for web serving workloads, demonstrating 15.32 GB/sec static web throughput, software compilation pipelines, microservices, and Redis caching instances capable of 16.49 million SET operations per second.
description: Microsoft Azure D8pls_v6 is an arm64 general purpose instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V, utilizing dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 cores at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 8 vCPUs from 8 physical cores without multithreading, configured with 16.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage volumes. In benchmark testing, the system demonstrates strong single-threaded gzip compression reaching 33.13 GB/sec, alongside middle-tier results in Geekbench multi-core at 9492.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 16568.19. Passmark encryption performance sits in the lower quartile, and 7B LLM prompt processing is limited to 12.34 tokens per second. Given its 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio and 15.32 GB/sec static web serving throughput, the configuration fits compute-centric web servers, continuous integration tasks, software compilation, and scalable microservices.
